processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: System modified to synthesize five different alloys in one operation; five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock; after cooling and cutting the blocks were 10 × 50 × 130 mm³.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: from 10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks to 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure (after hot rolling and water quenching) with a grain size of ~20 µm and some retained microsegregations of Mn; single-phase austenite at room temperature for the Al-free (0 wt.% Al) alloy.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Dislocation-based strain hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning is the primary strain-hardening mechanism (TWIP effect) for the single-phase austenitic SIMPLEX steel.
interfaces.interface_notes: Single-phase austenite at room temperature (Al < 5 wt.%); no phase interfaces reported for the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C reference.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; all plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Effect of 500 °C/24 h aging on YS, UTS, TE and hardness relative to the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE): YS virtually unchanged, hardness slightly increased, UTS and TE reduced (embrittlement).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.key_findings: For aged Fe-30Mn-1.2C (500 °C/24 h): YS virtually unchanged, hardness slightly increased, UTS and TE reduced (embrittlement).

characterization_methods.purpose: hardness screening across the RAP aging matrix
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness flat around 200 HBW over 0–6 wt.% Al; aging of Fe-30Mn-1.2C slightly increases hardness.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: As-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure prior to hot rolling (precursor state observed for the RAP materials).

The Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 wt.% Al) reference is a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel; its primary strain-hardening mechanism is dislocation-based strain hardening followed by mechanical twinning at higher loads.
Nominal composition of this sample: Fe-30Mn-1.2C (wt.%), no Al addition (x = 0 wt.% Al), i.e., the Al-free reference of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl screening.
